newsitem.title: Philippines: Philippine peso ends down on news of reserve cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on news of reserve cut.

text.p: * Volume thins to $126.10 million from $217.6 million
The Philippine peso ended weak on Friday at 26.288 from 26.282 as banks started to cover some of their short positions, traders said.
News that the Central Bank will cut reserve requirements next year by two percentage points is expected to nudge down the peso, prodding banks to buy dollars.
A Reuter poll showed the peso could hit an average of 26.60 to the dollar next year from the 1996 estimate of 26.22.
The peso was also pulled down by the swap points over the weekend as some banks sold dollars for same-day delivery and bought dollars for next-Monday delivery .
In this way, banks would have the peso that earn higher interest over the weekend, traders said.
"The peso was stable. It was just range trading," a dealer said, since the peso was within the Central Bank's desired range of 26.27 to 26.292.
The day's average, however, showed a stronger peso at 26.285 versus 26.287 because of trades for same-day delivery.
Next week, a dealer said, the peso could go either way in the range of 26.282 to 26.30.

The market is expected to be flooded with dollars from remittances of overseas contract workers. At the same time, there could be outflows of arbitrage money due to the lower interest rates in the domestic market, the same dealer said.
